sources_considered.why: Republished Intercom press release from March 2023. It shows an AI support bot built to hold full support conversations in a human-like tone. This bears on the 'mimic' part.

UC San Diego release on the JAMA Internal Medicine study. Raters judged ChatGPT's written replies more empathetic than doctors' replies. This is context on displayed empathy, in a medical setting rather than customer service.
Legal commentary quoting the 2024 Moffatt v. Air Canada tribunal decision: the company, not the chatbot, is responsible. This is context on responsibility. It comes after the post.

receipt.public_excerpt: Fin can hold complete support conversations with customers, understand complex queries, ask clarifying questions and explain complicated subjects clearly and in a human-like tone.

evidence_items.explanation: Shows that before the post, a vendor was selling an AI bot built to do a human support agent's visible work in a human-like tone. This fits the 'mimic' part. It is a company claim, not an independent test, and it says nothing about responsibility or felt empathy.

evidence_items.publisher: ScienceDaily (University of California - San Diego release)
evidence_items.locator: section 'Designing a Study to Test ChatGPT in a Healthcare Setting', final paragraph

receipt.public_excerpt: The responses were also more empathic: empathetic or very empathetic responses were 9.8 times higher for ChatGPT than for physicians (physicians 4.6% versus ChatGPT 45.1%).

evidence_items.explanation: Raters judged AI-written medical replies as showing more empathy than doctors' replies. This measures displayed empathy, which the speaker's word 'mimic' already concedes. It does not test whether the AI has empathy, and it is about medicine, not customer service.

evidence_items.publisher: Barry Sookman (legal commentary quoting the BC Civil Resolution Tribunal)
evidence_items.locator: quoted tribunal reasoning, before 'Comments on the decision'

receipt.public_excerpt: In effect, Air Canada suggests the chatbot is a separate legal entity that is responsible for its own actions. This is a remarkable submission. While a chatbot has an interactive component, it is still just a part of Air Canada’s website.

evidence_items.explanation: Shows that the chatbot itself was not treated as responsible; the company was. That matches the literal 'no responsibility' reading. It also cuts against the idea that AI lets a company escape responsibility. It comes after the post, so it is context only.

unresolved_gaps: No public evidence can show whether an AI agent feels empathy. That half of the claim is about inner states, not observable facts.
Whether the AI 'has responsibility' is either true by definition (software is not a legal person) or a judgment about how companies behave. Neither can be tested as a fact.
Found no independent test from before May 2023 of how well AI support agents matched human agents. The 'mimic' part rests on vendor claims.
